input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects identified by the accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — so that each flow is fully operable by keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible focus indicators.

## Scope

- Resolve every keyboard-operability defect enumerated in the audit report for the four audited flows: focus must be managed correctly when modals and dialogs open and close (focus moved into the dialog on open, restored to the triggering control on close), no focus traps, and no controls unreachable via keyboard navigation.
- Apply consistent visible focus indicators across all interactive controls in the four audited flows, replacing the inconsistent indicator styling the audit identified.
- Keyboard operability and focus-indicator consistency are delivered as one pass over the same flows and the same modal/focus-management code; they are not separately schedulable and are bundled in this epic.
- Where practical, extend the Dashboard's existing automated tests to cover keyboard-only completion of the audited flows so the fixes are regression-protected.
- Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using the keyboard alone.
- No focus traps remain in any modal or dialog within the audited flows; focus is restored to the triggering control when a modal closes.
- Every interactive control in the audited flows is reachable and operable by keyboard.
- Focus indicators are visually consistent across all interactive controls in the audited flows.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is resolved, or explicitly dispositioned with a recorded reason if out of scope.
- Automated tests covering keyboard-only completion of the four flows pass in the Dashboard's test suite where such coverage is practical.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by the keyboard-operability remediation in this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows — covered by the focus-indicator consistency work in this epic. Bundled with HLR-1: both requirements edit the same modals, focus-management code, and flow surfaces in the same component and team; splitting them would double-touch the same call sites.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates the accessibility conformance documentation for the Dashboard — the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product documentation accessibility statement — to reflect the fixed keyboard-accessibility state of the four core flows, and republishes both through the Red Hat docs content process. The updated, published conformance statement is a renewal requirement for two public-sector customers.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **VPAT update**: revise the conformance entries covering keyboard operability and focus visibility for the four remediated core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) so the documented conformance claims match the fixed state; update any entries the audit defects previously forced into non-conformance or partial-conformance wording.
- **Accessibility statement update**: revise the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the current supported keyboard-accessibility state of the audited flows.
- **Republish**: run both updated documents through the Red Hat docs content process to publication.
- Out of scope: conformance claims for flows outside the four audited ones, and screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes delivered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT's entries for the four audited flows reflect the implemented keyboard-operability and focus-indicator fixes, with no claims contradicting the delivered state.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated and republished to match.
- Both documents are technically reviewed against the implemented Dashboard fixes by the engineering team that delivered them, and review findings are addressed before publication.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are published and live at their documented locations.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review — this epic delivers that documentation in full.

Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows.

## Triage Analysis

Step 0 Check 1 (below-threshold) was evaluated and rejected: although the strategy is small and the Dashboard fixes themselves would score High AI implementability, the scope spans two architecturally distinct work streams — Dashboard code remediation and substantive documentation authoring (VPAT rewrite and accessibility statement republication) — that warrant separate PR review cycles. Check 2 (documentation-only) does not apply: Dashboard requires code changes. Decomposition proceeds through Steps 1-8.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001: Dashboard keyboard remediation] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002: VPAT and accessibility statement update]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The conformance documentation must describe the fixed state of the four flows; it cannot be authored or technically reviewed until the Dashboard remediation is complete. |

No other edges: there is a single Implementation epic for the code work, no investigations (the strategy states there are no open questions — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow), no external dependencies, and no new components (Dashboard is in the platform inventory; Documentation is a canonical Jira component for docs-authoring work). No konflux-onboarding, license-validation, or repo-onboarding epics are needed — the Dashboard already exists as a Konflux-onboarded component per its architecture-context file.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | docs-authoring epic; priority derived via the Step 4 exception (strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` → P2), not inherited from E001. |

All three HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Component Mapping

Both strategy components map verbatim to canonical names in `.context/rhai-components.txt`: `Dashboard` and `Documentation`. No non-obvious mappings.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no formal Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then), and no Non-Functional Requirements. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs and the problem statement. Teams were inferred: RHOAI Dashboard from the Dashboard architecture-context file (`architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`); the Documentation epic's team ("RHOAI Documentation") is an inference — the strategy names no owning team for documentation. Verify team assignment before submission.
- **E001 size / re-split trigger**: the keyboard-accessibility remediation epic bundles keyboard operability for the four audited flows, focus-indicator consistency, and test-extension coverage into one epic that sits at or near the ~2-week guideline. This is one logical pass over one surface (the Dashboard modal and focus-management code shared by the four flows) by one team, so it is not split now; a split would double-touch the same call sites. **Re-split trigger**: if the audit defect count across the four flows exceeds a sprint of Dashboard remediation effort, split the epic along per-flow lines (one epic per audited flow: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission), each carrying its portion of the HLR-1/HLR-2 scope and acceptance criteria.
- **No priority inversions detected**: HLR-1/HLR-2 are P1 code fixes; HLR-3 is P2 documentation, correctly sequenced after the fixes it describes.
- **No scope traps detected**: out-of-scope items (screen-reader semantics beyond keyboard fixes, flows outside the four audited ones) do not contradict any requirement.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — there are no external dependencies with uncertain timing. The two epics run strictly serially (code fixes, then documentation of the fixed state).
